findings.title: Stats table merges harvests of different plants that share a name
findings.where: GET /api/stats/harvests (backend/routers/stats.py, GROUP BY p.name, month) and /stats table
findings.steps: Have plant 'Tomato · Sungold' (450 g in Jul 2026, 600 g in Aug 2026). Create a second plant 'Tomato' variety 'Gardeners Delight' and log 2000 g on 2026-07-10. Open /stats.
findings.expected: Sungold row: Jul 450 g, Aug 600 g, total 1.05 kg; Gardeners Delight row: Jul 2 kg, total 2 kg (matches the Best plants list).
findings.actual: Gardeners Delight row shows Jul 2.45 kg / total 2.45 kg, and Sungold row shows only Aug 600 g / total 600 g. Sungold's July harvest is credited to the other Tomato, so the table disagrees with Best plants (2 kg and 1.05 kg).
findings.evidence: API plants: [{plant_id 4, Gardeners Delight, total 2450, monthly [0,2450,0,0]}, {plant_id 1, Sungold, total 600}] while top_plants says 4→2000, 1→1050. The query groups by p.name instead of p.id.

findings.title: Stats page crashes on a response it can't read (non-JSON or missing fields)
findings.steps: Mock GET /api/stats/harvests to return 200 with body '<html>oops</html>' (text/html) or '{}'. On the dashboard, click 'Stats' in the nav.
findings.expected: An error state saying the stats could not be loaded, with a retry option.
findings.actual: The page never renders. The URL changes to /stats but the dashboard stays on screen, and nothing tells the user it failed.
findings.evidence: Console: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length') at stats.vue render (stats.plants.length). #main innerText still showed the Dashboard.

findings.title: Null fields in the response show as 'null harvests'
findings.steps: Mock /api/stats/harvests with harvest_count:null, total_grams:null, date_from:null, top_plants:null and so on, then open Stats from the nav.
findings.expected: Fall back cleanly or show an error.
findings.actual: The page shows 'null harvests from – to –' and an empty 'Best plants' heading.
findings.evidence:
#main text: 'null harvests from – to –

Best plants
Weight by plant and month
– total'

findings.title: Stats request has no timeout, so the page shows 'Loading stats…' forever
findings.steps: Make /api/stats/harvests hang (never respond), then change the From date.
findings.expected: The request fails after 10 s and an error with a retry option appears.
findings.actual: After 13 s the page still showed 'Loading stats…' and kept the old table. No timeout is set on useApiFetch.

findings.title: Error state has no retry button
findings.steps: Make /api/stats/harvests return 500, open Stats from the nav, then bring the API back.
findings.expected: The error message comes with a Retry button that reloads the stats.
findings.actual: The page shows only 'Could not load harvest stats.' and there are no buttons in main. The only way to recover is to edit a date field or reload the page.
findings.evidence: Buttons in #main: []. Template has an AlertMessage with no refresh() action.

findings.title: Clearing a date field silently uses this year's date and can give a confusing error
findings.steps: Open /stats?from=2025-01-01&to=2025-12-31 and clear the From field.
findings.expected: A blank field is either refused with a clear reason or treated as 'no lower bound'.
findings.actual: The client drops the parameter, so the server uses 2026-01-01. The page then says 'The From date must be on or before the To date.' even though From is empty. If To is in this year, blank From quietly means 1 Jan this year.
findings.evidence: Observed error text 'The From date must be on or before the To date.' with an empty From input.

findings.title: Invalid date in the URL shows a raw validation message and a blank field
findings.expected: A readable message, or falling back to the default range.
findings.actual: The From input is blank and the error reads 'Query.from: Input should be a valid date or datetime, day value is outside expected range'.

findings.title: Dashboard top plant shows only the name, which is ambiguous for plants with the same name
findings.steps: With two 'Tomato' plants (Sungold and Gardeners Delight), look at the dashboard card.
findings.expected: Enough detail to tell which plant it is (the variety), or a link to that plant.
findings.actual: The card shows just 'Tomato · 2 kg harvested' and links to /stats, not to the plant. top_plant_id is returned but not used.
